events.comment: Combat_Shared: rules used by every fight. Each scene needs an Enemy group and an EnemyHitbox group, and links this sheet before that boss's own events. Every EnemyHitbox object needs Damage, HasHit and IsMelee variables.
Arena fade-in: every fight (and the tutorial) opens from black: a short hold, then a smooth fade of about a second.
Scene start: remember the uncursed max HP and set up the bar maximums. (Where the bars sit is the fight UI layout's job, further down.)
Boss reaction flags: true for one frame. Each boss's events read them right after this sheet.
Remove blood effects when their animation ends.
Remove the deflect spark when its animation ends.
Show the rally bar while rally HP is pending.
Hide the rally bar when no rally HP is pending.
Update every bar value.
Player deleted: empty the HP bar and hide the rally bar.
Cursed HP bar: while cursed, size the black sprite to the max HP lost and pin it to the right end of the HP fill.
Cursed HP bar: no curse, so hide the black sprite.
Curse icons: one flame per curse on the player, in a row next to the stamina bar. Curse_Icon is a tiled sprite, so its width sets how many show.
Curse icons: no curse, so hide them.

Fight UI layout: the player's bars top-left (posture only while above zero), the boss's name, life marks, posture and HP in a block at the bottom centre. It runs after every event each frame, so it overrides where the boss sheets put the bars; they still show and hide them.
Enemy posture slowly recovers after 1.5 seconds without being hit.
Keep enemy posture within its maximum.
Enemy dodges this hit: no damage. Sets JustDodgedHit so the boss can react.

Player hits the enemy, once per swing: damage, posture, blood, rally healing, and a hit sound. Sets JustHitByPlayer for the boss's events. Skipped while Enemy.Invulnerable is true. Also adds hit-stop and screen shake.
The hit came from a lunge: add LungeBonusDamage and set JustStaggered for the boss events.
Enemy posture break: starts the stun and sets JustPostureBroken for the boss's events. Also adds a strong hit-stop and screen shake.
Enemy stun ends after Enemy.StunDuration seconds and sets JustRecovered for the boss's events.

Deathblow: press F in melee range of a posture-broken enemy. The player winds up, then cuts. The cut removes one enemy life, and the curse lifts as the life wisps reach the player. The player is locked and cannot be hit until it finishes. Also adds a strong hit-stop and screen shake on the cut.
Enemy on the right: dash right.
Enemy on the left: dash left.
Wall check: pass through only if the landing spot, DeathblowPassDist past the enemy, is inside DeathblowMinX to DeathblowMaxX. Otherwise the cut happens in front of him and the player stays put.
Room behind the enemy: pass through.
Deathblow cut, on the dash frame: the hit itself, the orb shatter and the slash. The player then glows crimson as the life is taken.
Pass through: land DeathblowPassDist past the enemy, still facing the same way, so the player ends with their back to him. The slash runs from where they started to where they land.
Wall behind the enemy: no pass. The slash runs from the player across the enemy.
Deathblow: hold the follow-through, blade forward, for DeathblowHold seconds.
Deathblow: the hold is over, so he raises the blade, slowly, to clean it.
Deathblow: the blade is up. Pause there for DeathblowRaiseHold seconds, the moment before the flick.
Deathblow: the pause is over, so flick the blood off in one fast swish, then settle.
Deathblow finished: give control back.

Deathblow glow: for DeathblowGlowTime seconds the player glows crimson, fading back, as the stolen life flows in. When it ends, the curse lifts and HP refills (DeathblowLanded, handled by the curse removal event below).
Early in the glow: deep crimson.
Later in the glow: fading toward normal.
Glow over: back to normal, and the life lands.
Remove the orb shatter and the slash when their animations end.
Remove the slash when its animation ends.
Deathblow prompt: the orb, hidden by default. Uses the same conditions as the deathblow, minus the key press.
Deathblow prompt: show the orb just above the enemy's head when a deathblow is possible. Enemy.DeathblowOrbDrop lowers it for a boss whose stunned pose is shorter than its collision box.
Enemy loses a life at 0 HP and sets JustLostLife. On its last life it is deleted, or sets JustDied if HasDeathAnimation is on.

Deflect: an enemy attack that reaches the player within DeflectWindow seconds of raising the sword is stopped, with a random clash sound and a burst of sparks (one of the Deflect_Spark animations, picked at random). Setting HasHit makes the damage event below skip it. All enemy attacks go through this, including each Thousand Cuts slash. Also adds hit-stop and screen shake. One press stops any number of melee attacks, but only one ranged attack (DeflectRangedUsed), so each arrow of a double shot needs its own deflect. Both branches of that Or name EnemyHitbox and Player on purpose: an Or only keeps the objects its true branches picked, so a branch that left one out would drop it (no arrow blocked, or no Player to act on).

Deflect sound: one of the 21 echo clashes at random (7 pitches x 3 takes, made by tools/fx/clash.js), so repeated deflects never sound identical. Replaces sword_parry_01.wav. Also draws the new spark additively, so its glow lights up its surroundings.
Deflected a melee attack: it also adds DeflectPostureDamage to the enemy posture and stops posture recovery for a moment, like a hit does. Attacks with IsMelee off, such as ranged ones, add nothing.
Deflected a ranged attack (an arrow, a rain hit): this press is used up for ranged attacks, so a second arrow close behind it needs its own deflect.

Enemy attack hits the player once per attack object. Damage comes from that object's Damage variable, and JustHitPlayer is set for the boss's events. A hit also drops any saved action, cancels the player attack, deflect or roll (a roll only gets hit once its i-frames are over) and plays the Player_Hit reaction. Also adds hit-stop and screen shake. Nothing can hit the player during a grab, so a stray attack cannot break that animation.
Player loses a life: applies the curse (one more CurseStacks), clears rally and posture, and starts respawn invulnerability. On the last life, the player dies instead.
Last life gone: play the death animation. The player is locked and cannot be hit, and the fade below returns to the hub.
End respawn invulnerability after 1.5 seconds.
Player death: DeathHold seconds after the collapse, fade the screen to black over DeathFadeTime seconds.
Player death fade: darken, keep it over the camera, and go back to the hub once it is black.
Player death fade is black: back to the hub.
Curse removal: the deathblow sets Player.DeathblowLanded. This restores max HP, clears CurseStacks, refills HP, and clears rally.
Player status, root: while RootLeft lasts the player cannot move, roll or lunge, but can still attack and deflect. Player_Movement checks IsRooted.
Root over.
Player status, poison: while PoisonLeft lasts, the player loses PoisonTick HP every half second and is tinted purple. Death ends it.
Every half second: lose PoisonTick HP. PoisonAcc counts the time, because a timer that was never started never passes its check.
Poison over: back to the normal colour.
Debug: F5 restarts the current scene. Remove before release.

Boss beaten: when every enemy in the Enemy group is dead and its death animation has settled, wait a moment, fade to black, mark the boss as beaten (BossesBeaten), note this fight in JustBeaten (the hub starts the player at its gate) and return to HUB_Area.

inlineCode: // Boss beaten: once every enemy in the scene's Enemy group has died and settled (its death animation on its last frame,
// or deleted), wait HOLD seconds, fade to black over FADE seconds and go back to the hub.
// Scenes that never had a living enemy (the hub, the templates) never trigger it. A dying player wins over it.
const HOLD = 2.5; // Seconds to look at the fallen boss before the fade.
const FADE = 1.2; // Seconds for the fade to black.
const MAX_SETTLE = 20; // Seconds: stop waiting for a death animation that never reaches its last frame.
const st = runtimeScene.__victory || (runtimeScene.__victory = { names: null, seen: false, settle: 0, hold: 0, fade: 0, overlay: null });
for (const name of st.names) for (const o of runtimeScene.getObjects(name)) {
if (runtimeScene.getObjects("Player_Death_Fade").length > 0) return; // The player died too: the death fade handles it.
const dt = time.getElapsedTime() / 1000 / time.getTimeScale(); // Real seconds, through hit-stops.
if (dying > 0 && st.settle < MAX_SETTLE) { st.settle += dt; return; }
// Fade: a black rectangle over everything, on the UI layer (or the base layer in scenes without one).
// Remember the win for the hub, which shows this boss's gate as completed (until the game is closed).
// And which fight we just won, so the hub can start the player at its gate and play the defeat cutscene.

events.comment: Hit-stop and screen shake: runs last, so effects started on this frame apply right away. Tune them with the HitStop and Shake variables on the Player.

inlineCode: // Hit-stop and screen shake. Events start them by setting HitStopLeft, ShakeLeft and ShakeStrength on the Player, in real seconds.
const STOP_TIME_SCALE = 0.05; // Game speed during a hit-stop. Not 0, so the elapsed time stays usable.
const SHAKE_LAYERS = ["Background", ""]; // The UI layer stays still.
// Where the camera rests when not shaking. A scene with a moving camera (the hub's follow) sets runtimeScene.__cameraBase
// each frame before this runs, so the shake happens around it. Fight scenes don't, so they rest at the screen centre.
const base = runtimeScene.__cameraBase || { x: centerX, y: centerY };
// Player deleted: nothing can end the effects any more, so end them here.
// Elapsed time is scaled by the game speed, so undo that to count in real seconds.
